data.title: Domestic flyers also subject to new luggage search rule
data.description: Travellers on all domestic flights are also liable to have their luggage searched under new regulations, not just flyers leaving the kingdom, the Civil Aviation Authority of Thailand (CAAT) warned on Sunday.

data.title: Flooding persists in Bangkok, 17 provinces, toll at 83
data.description: Flooding persisted in parts of Bangkok and in 17 provinces, mostly in the Central Plains, but water levels were declining, the Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation reported on Sunday.

data.title: B40/day fare on Red, Purple lines likely to be extended
data.description: The Transport Ministry will propose the extension of the 40-baht day-tripper rate on the two Red Lines and the Purple line for another year, with the current promotion due to end on Nov 30.

data.title: Heavy rain in Northeast, North, Central Plains, East, South early this week
data.description: The Meteorological Department forecast is for fluctuating weather and possible heavy rain in the Northeast, North, Central Plains and East into Tuesday, and persistent rain in the South into Wednesday.

data.title: Missing Dutch celebrity left Thailand late last year - police
data.description: Missing Dutch television personality and politician Emile Ratelband, whose family is seeking information as to his whereabouts, left Thailand late last year, according to immigration police.

data.title: 'No ID, No Ads' looms
data.description: The government is intensifying its crackdown on online scams with a new "No ID, No Ads" policy taking effect on Nov 1.

data.title: Airports told to brace for rain
data.description: The Department of Airports has been instructed to prepare its facilities in the South for heavy rain, deputy government spokeswoman Ploythalay Laksameesaengjan says.

data.title: PM reaffirms commitment to global peace on UN Day
data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has reaffirmed Thailand's commitment to international law, peaceful dispute resolution and global cooperation in a speech marking United Nations Day.

data.title: Navy insists on fair probe into conscript's death
data.description: The Royal Thai Navy has pledged not to shield anyone found to have committed wrongdoing in connection with the death of a conscript during training in 2024, following findings by the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) that he was assaulted and denied timely medical treatment.

data.title: Chanthaburi border fence phase one done
data.description: The first phase of the security fence at the Thai-Cambodian border is finished, while the next phases are progressing, according to local security units.

data.title: Social media guidelines given to NACC staff
data.description: The National Anti-Corruption Commission (NACC) has issued new guidelines restricting officials' use of social media during working hours and prohibiting online conduct that could undermine the agency's reputation and public confidence.

data.title: Governors to collect royal fireboxes on Nov 20
data.description: Interior permanent secretary Unsit Sampuntharat has ordered provincial governors to collect royal fireboxes at Government House on Nov 20 for public sandalwood-flower offerings honouring the late Queen Mother.

data.title: Agriculture dept to review holy basil registration bid
data.description: Agriculture and Cooperatives Minister Suriya Juangroongruangkit has ordered an investigation into a company's application for plant variety protection covering four holy basil varieties, amid concerns the move could affect farmers' rights and traditional cultivation practices.

data.title: GDP will beat 2.1%  forecast, PM says
data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has ordered the Office of the National Economic and Social Development Council (NESDC) to reassess its GDP outlook after key economic indicators improved.

data.title: FM praises 'progress' on Suu Kyi
data.description: Foreign Affairs Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow on Saturday welcomed Myanmar's decision to allow detained former leader Aung San Suu Kyi to speak to her son for the first time in more than five years, calling it a sign of progress.

data.title: Education award recipients share innovative ideas
data.description: Recipients of this year’s Princess Maha Chakri Award showcased their innovative approaches to education at a recent international conference presided over by Her Royal Highness Princess Maha Chakri Sirindhorn.

data.title: Motorcyclist held for road rage attack on Bangkok woman
data.description: A 19-year-old motorcyclist who smashed a car windscreen and punched a 27-year-old woman in the face during a road rage incident at the Lat Phrao intersection in Bangkok has been remanded in custody.

data.title: Anutin leaves door open to third coalition partner
data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has not ruled out bringing a third major party into the coalition government, saying anything is possible in politics if it serves the national interest and strengthens government stability.

data.title: Israeli accused of making sex videos after serving drug-laced cake
data.description: Police have arrested a 54-year-old Israeli man accused of serving drug-laced cake to women he met through a dating app before having sex with them and filming videos.

data.title: Bangkok seeks to keep control of southern peace process
data.description: Thailand has welcomed Malaysia's appointment of a new peace dialogue facilitator for the southern border provinces, but insists that Bangkok must retain control over the peace process and its overall direction.

data.title: University defends holy basil protection
data.description: Kasetsart University has defended legal protection for four new varieties of holy basil, or kaprao, saying registration does not automatically restrict farmers from growing other varieties.

data.title: House speaker calls for deal on censure debate
data.description: House Speaker Sophon Zarum has urged government and opposition whips to reach a compromise on the schedule for a no-confidence debate, saying the opposition was willing to reduce its demand from five days to four if the debate was held in November or December.

data.title: Woman and child saved from knife-wielding hostage taker
data.description: A woman and child were rescued after being taken hostage by a man, reportedly the child’s father, who threatened them with a knife near a flyover on Phetchaburi Road in Bangkok on Saturday morning.

data.title: Relocation aid offered to Uthenthawai students and staff
data.description: The Ministry of Higher Education has said it will cut tuition fees by 50% and arrange alternative laboratories for students affected by the pending relocation of the Uthenthawai Campus of Rajamangala University of Technology Tawan-ok.

data.title: Orange shadow looms over People’s Party
data.description: The recent warning by former Future Forward Party secretary-general Piyabutr Saengkanokkul that the People’s Party (PP) should not allow politics to descend into “entertainocracy” is more than a criticism of political communication. It also highlights a lingering reality for the main opposition party: the political shadow of its predecessor remains difficult to escape.

data.title: Phiphat tells Maxbit to clarify claims
data.description: Transport Minister Phiphat Ratchakitprakarn has urged Maxbit to explain reported transfers to gambling platform Shuffle.com after former MP Sirichok Sopha questioned the digital asset broker, partly owned by Mr Phiphat's son.

data.title: Orange shadow looms over PP
data.description: The recent warning by former Future Forward Party (FFP) secretary-general Piyabutr Saengkanokkul that the People's Party (PP) should not allow politics to descend into "entertainocracy" is more than a criticism of political communication. It also highlights a lingering reality for the PP: the political shadow of its predecessor remains difficult to escape.

data.title: 2 Chinese Uyghurs pardoned
data.description: Two Chinese Uyghur men detained in Thailand have received royal pardons and are awaiting deportation, a Thai official and an activist said on Thursday, though it was not yet clear where they will go.

data.title: NHRC faults navy over conscript's death
data.description: The National Human Rights Commission has ruled that delays in providing medical treatment to a navy conscript who died during training violated his right to timely healthcare, recommending compensation for his family and reforms to prevent similar cases.

data.title: Ministry offers aid over campus move
data.description: The Higher Education, Science, Research and Innovation Ministry has said it will cut tuition fees by 50% and arrange alternative laboratories for students affected by the relocation of Rajamangala University of Technology Tawan-ok's Uthenthawai Campus.

data.title: Lorry driver arrested over suspected waste dumping
data.description: Police have arrested a truck driver and seized an 18-wheel lorry carrying suspected industrial waste allegedly destined for illegal dumping in Sa Kaeo.

data.title: Govt proposes changes to snooker and boxing rules
data.description: The government has opened a month-long public consultation on gambling regulation amendments to ease youth snooker restrictions and modernise boxing competition rules.

data.title: Irish ties set for fresh push
data.description: Chiang Mai is seeking closer ties with Ireland in tourism, agriculture and trade to boost economic and cultural links.

data.title: Uni defends holy basil patents
data.description: Kasetsart University has defended legal protection for four new holy basil, or kaprao, varieties, saying registration does not automatically restrict farmers from growing other varieties.
